title: Quantum Gravity Testability (Banks' Verification Limit)
bottleneck: Tom Banks argued that no quantum gravity model in a de Sitter-like universe can be verified to arbitrary precision by any observer inside it — competing models may be empirically indistinguishable forever. If correct, quantum gravity faces an in-principle epistemic ceiling, not merely a technological one. If some quantum gravity models are observationally indistinguishable even in principle, theory selection must rely on non-empirical criteria like mathematical consistency.
why_it_blocks: This would make the search for quantum gravity partly a mathematical rather than empirical enterprise, with no experiment able to crown a winner.
current_state: The argument is debated but unrefuted; it sharpens the demand for any quantum gravity proposal to state its observable consequences precisely. This prospect forces physicists to confront what counts as scientific knowledge when experiments cannot decide.
